docs.title: Neuroscience Control
docs.text:
neuroscience-control is a PyTorch toolkit for whole-brain resting-state fMRI modeling. It provides three model families with a shared training and evaluation pipeline:

  • Coupled Hopf (physics-informed oscillators)
  • Hybrid Hopf (Hopf + learnable coupling network)
  • Neural SDE (data-driven stochastic dynamics)

docs.title: Why this package
docs.text:
• Complex-valued dynamical systems support for state and noise
  • Reproducible training pipelines (grid search, backprop, paper run)
  • Domain metrics out of the box: FC, FCD, phFCD, metastability, and timeseries fit
  • Ready for package publishing to TestPyPI/PyPI and docs deployment via GitHub Pages

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: This repository includes automated workflows for CI, docs, and release publishing.

docs.title: Local preflight
docs.text:
Run these before creating a release:

uv sync --group dev --group docs
uv run pytest --cov=src --cov=neuroscience_control --cov-report=term-missing
uv run mkdocs build --strict
uv run python -m build
uv run twine check dist/*

docs.title: TestPyPI publish (manual)
docs.text: Use Actions -> Publish -> Run workflow. This triggers the publish-testpypi job.

docs.title: PyPI publish (release)
docs.text: Create a GitHub Release tag (for example v0.2.0). On release: published, workflow uploads dist/* to PyPI.

docs.title: Required repository setup
docs.text:
1. Configure PyPI and TestPyPI trusted publishing for this repo.
  2. Create GitHub Environments: testpypi and pypi.
  3. Configure Codecov for coverage badge/reporting.
  4. Ensure main is your default release branch.

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text:
Current public modules:

  • neuroscience_control.dataset
  • neuroscience_control.models
  • neuroscience_control.training
  • neuroscience_control.metrics
  • neuroscience_control.utils

docs.title: Import examples
docs.text:
from neuroscience_control.models import CoupledHopfModel, HybridHopfModel, NeuralSDE
from neuroscience_control.training import HopfConfig, NeuralSDEConfig, run_backprop_training
from neuroscience_control.metrics import compute_all_fc_metrics, compute_dynamics_fit_metrics

docs.title: Backwards compatibility
docs.text:
Legacy imports continue to work:

from src.models import CoupledHopfModel

Use neuroscience_control.* in new code.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.13+
  • Linux/macOS/Windows
  • Optional CUDA-enabled GPU for training speed

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
pip install neuroscience-control

Or with uv:

uv add neuroscience-control

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/dani2442/neuroscience_control.git
cd neuroscience_control
uv sync

docs.title: Verify installation
docs.text: python -c "import neuroscience_control as nc; print(nc.__version__)"

docs.title: Dependency notes
docs.text: uv is configured to use your torchsde fork through tool.uv.sources. If you install with plain pip, it will use the PyPI torchsde release.

docs.title: First Training Run
docs.text: This tutorial runs one short backprop experiment and saves outputs locally.

docs.title: 1. Prepare data
docs.text:
By default, training config points to:

data/ts_young/ts_young_TR0.72.mat

If your dataset path differs, edit TrainingConfig.data_path in src/training/config.py.

docs.title: 2. Run a quick experiment
docs.text:
python examples/train_models.py backprop \
  --model hopf \
  --n-epochs 2 \
  --no-wandb \
  --device cpu

docs.title: 3. Outputs
docs.text:
• Checkpoints: checkpoints/
  • Figures: paper/images/
  • Optional metrics JSON if you run the paper subcommand

docs.title: 4. Reproduce paper pipeline
docs.text:
python examples/train_models.py paper \
  --output-json results/paper_metrics.json \
  --no-wandb

This executes:

  1. Hopf grid search
  2. Backprop training for Hopf, Hybrid Hopf, and Neural SDE
  3. Metrics comparison report

docs.title: Metrics Evaluation
docs.text: The package includes static FC, dynamics, and timeseries metrics.

docs.title: Example: FC + dynamics metrics
docs.text:
import torch
from neuroscience_control.metrics import compute_all_fc_metrics, compute_dynamics_fit_metrics

# sim_ts and real_ts: [batch, n_rois, n_timepoints], complex-valued
sim_fc = torch.corrcoef(sim_ts.real[0])
real_fc = torch.corrcoef(real_ts.real[0])

fc_metrics = compute_all_fc_metrics(sim_fc.unsqueeze(0), real_fc.unsqueeze(0))
dyn_metrics = compute_dynamics_fit_metrics(
    sim_ts,
    real_ts,
    tr=0.72,
    fcd_win_sec=30.0,
    fcd_step_sec=2.0,
)

print(fc_metrics)
print(dyn_metrics)

docs.title: Key metrics used in training/evaluation
docs.text:
• fc_correlation
  • fc_mse
  • fcd_ks
  • phfcd_ks
  • metastability_diff
  • temporal_correlation
  • power_spectrum_distance
  • autocorr_distance

These metrics are aggregated in neuroscience_control.utils.EVAL_METRIC_KEYS.
